page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture running at 2.7 GHz. It features 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is equipped with 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU physics tests scoring in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, achieving top-tier status in both read and write operations for large blocks. Single-core performance, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, sits in the average tier. The server excels in database operations, static web serving throughput, and multi-threaded decompression, while showing weaker performance in LLM text generation tasks.

Given its bare-metal architecture, high core density, and massive integrated NVMe storage, this instance offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high-throughput local storage and parallel processing without virtualization overhead. It is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-concurrency web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
